Her practice engages themes of ancestral technology, intelligence, memory, and radical imagination. She has exhibited internationally, including at the 36th São Paulo Biennial in Brazil, the Congo Biennial (2025), and the inaugural Malta Biennial (2024). Her current solo exhibitions are on view at the Utah Museum of Fine Arts (September 13, 2025 - June 14, 2026) and the Harvey Gantt Center for African American Art & Culture in Charlotte, NC (October 3, 2025 - March 8, 2026)..Fawundu is the co-author of the critically acclaimed book MFON: Women Photographers of the African Diaspora. She is the recipient of numerous honors, including the Guggenheim Fellowship, CatchLight Fellowship, Anonymous Was A Woman Award, and the Rema Hort Mann Artist Grant. Her work is held in the permanent collections of the Brooklyn Museum of Art, Princeton University Art Museum, Newark Museum of Art, Portland Museum of Art, Bryn Mawr College, Norton Museum of Art, and the David C. Driskell Center. She is also an Assistant Professor of Visual Arts at Columbia University.

item.title: Adeleke Femi
item.description: Adeleke Femi is a Nigerian visual artist who hails from Osun State, known for his expressionist style. His paintings explore awakenened memories and familiar sensations, often giving voice to personal emotions, fear, aspirations and dreams.A gradaute of the University of Lagos with a Niational Diploma from the Polytechnic of Ibadan, Femi has exhibited in several notable shows, including Plus234 Art Fair, Total Energy, Emerging Expression, An Ode to Odd (Madhouse), Brushstrokes of Hope, Boundaries and Bridges (Iriri Art Gallery), Unbound (Creathlab), Becoming More etc.

item.title: Aksah Seyoum
item.description: Aksah Seyoum is a dedicated printmaker with a bachelor's degree in printmaking from Alle University, where she refined her technical skills and broadened her artistic vision. Her work celebrates Ethiopian culture, exploring themes of identity, tradition, and the connection between modern life and ancestral heritage. Aksah's intricate designs and precise techniques bring stories to life, reflecting both personal and collective experiences. She is particularly drawn to scarification patterns, using them as a medium to express her fascination with cultural traditions. Each mark tells a unique story, making her work a meaningful exploration of art, culture, and narrative. . . .

item.title: Alexia Smit
item.description: Alexia Smit is a painter and scholar whose work explores how Cape Town is represented on South African television. Using paint as a research tool, she reinterprets scenes from local dramas to reveal social and spatial inequalities. Her series inspired by Skemerdans portrays a more familiar, working-class cityscape rather than the glossy images often shown on screen. Holding a PhD in Film and Television Studies, she integrates visual research with cultural theory. Smit is currently collaborating with colleagues at the University of Cape Town to produce illustrated zines on South African visual culture.

item.title: Alsadig Mahmoud
item.description: Alsadig Mahmoud (born 1983, Khartoum North, Sudan) is a Sudanese multidisciplinary artist whose work draws deeply from Sudanese culture and symbolism to reflect the experiences of his people both at home and in exile. Blending painting, drawing, collage, and sculpture, he creates visual narratives that explore peace, conflict, humanity, and hope.His compositions often merge architectural forms, figures, and natural elements, capturing a poetic harmony between movement and memory. Mahmoud has exhibited in Transformations: New Perspectives (Nairobi), Nordic Encounters (Stockholm), Anthropology of Detachment (Nairobi), Home: A Daydream (Nairobi), and Echos of Place (Kampala). He currently lives and works in Nairobi, Kenya.

item.title: Amani Azhari
item.description: Amani Azhari Amani Azhari; (b.1998) visual artist from Sudan, received her bachelor's in fine and Applied Arts in 2022 from University of Sudan. and participated in numerous internal exhibitions in her home country. After obtaining her Bachelor's degree in Fine and Applied Arts from the University of Sudan in 2022, she ventured to Kampala, Uganda.Continuing her artistic journey through residencies and exhibitions, she has recently been painting from her studio in Nairobi, Kenya. Amani finds inspiration in girls' sessions, where they express their thoughts and experiences in a society that often silences them with numerous restrictions. Through these sessions, she shares blame, fears, and even beautiful sentiments that are difficult to disclose publicly. Utilizing girls as a fundamental element in her expression, she draws from her personal features to strengthen her message.

item.title: Annette Faul
item.description: Annette Faul is a South African artist based in Stellenbosch, known for her botanical art, maps, and landscape drawings. Her work captures ephemeral moments in nature, with a focus on plants and seasonal transformations.Faul studied Landscape Architecture at the University of Pretoria and the University of Cape Town, and completed a botanical art masterclass with Beverley Allen. Her paintings, such as Bokkeveld in August, celebrate the changing seasons, the interplay of biomes, and the vivid colors of indigenous flora. Through meticulous brushstrokes and detailed observation, she evokes a sense of belonging, awe, and memory in the landscapes of the Western and Northern Cape.

item.title: Billie Zangewa
item.description: Billie Zangewa is a contemporary visual artist best known for her intricate hand-sewn silk collages. Her work draws deeply from personal experiences, exploring themes of gender, domestic labour, and racial prejudice. Through delicate textile compositions, Zangewa portrays intimate scenes of everyday life, often centered on her identity and the emotional landscape of Black womanhood. Her art transforms the personal into the political, creating powerful narratives that celebrate resilience, self-representation, and empowerment.

item.title: Blen Deresse
item.description: Blen Deresse is an Addis Ababa-based painter exploring psychological tension through atmospheric compositions. Transitioning from fashion to fine arts, her work captures emotional paralysis, balancing gesture and negative space to reveal the fragile line between comfort and constraint. Her paintings serve as mirrors of unspoken struggles, establishing her as a rising voice in contemporary art.Deresse's practice is marked by a restrained yet evocative visual language, where figures often appear suspended between motion and stillness, echoing states of hesitation, withdrawal, or quiet resistance. Her background in fashion continues to inform her sensitivity to form, texture, and the body, translating into paintings that feel both intimate and distanced at once. By allowing negative space to carry as much weight as her figures, she creates compositions that breathe with tension, inviting viewers to sit with discomfort rather than resolve it. Through this delicate interplay, Deresse's work speaks to broader, often unspoken experiences of anxiety, isolation, and emotional restraint, positioning her practice within a growing dialogue on mental and psychological wellbeing in contemporary African art.

item.title: Bubu Ogisi and Mbali Dhlamini
item.description: Bubu Ogisi and Mbali Dhlamini are multidisciplinary African artists whose practices explore materiality, decolonization, and indigenous knowledge systems. Ogisi, a Lagos-born fibre artist and Creative Director of I.AM.ISIGO, creates gravity-defying textile works that challenge Eurocentric design norms. Dhlamini, a visual researcher from South Africa, investigates African identity through visual, tactile, and linguistic forms, reworking colonial imagery to reveal cultural resilience and indigenous philosophies. Together, their work embodies a dialogue between tradition, material transformation, and contemporary thought.

item.title: Carine Mansan
item.description: Carine Mansan (b. 1988, born in Côte d’Ivoire) is sculptor and painter who lives and works in Grand Bassam in Ivory Coast. Born to an Ivorian mother and a French father, she grew up lulled by two cultures. In the Ivory Coast, she spent most of her childhood and adolescence before continuing her studies in France and Montreal.After obtaining a diploma in Interior design at the Ecole de Condé in Paris and then at the University of Montreal, she devoted herself entirely to painting and drawing. She began exhibiting her works in Montreal in 2015. Over the years, she has participated in numerous cultural events at other international venues. Her works are in reputable private collections around the world. Today Mansan’s work is about the feminine image; it is figurative, covering sculpture and realist paintings of portraits and everyday life. She is currently our first Ivory Coast Visiting Fellow at the Noldor Residency for the 2021 year.

item.title: Chantal Masinga
item.description: Chantal Masinga is an oil painter whose intuitive practice explores emotion, perception, and the self through layered, meditative processes. Working in monochrome and limited palettes, she focuses on texture, form, and emotional depth.Her painting Breath Between the Clouds captures a quiet moment of reflection amid lifes chaos  dark tones evoking mental weight and soft pinks suggesting calm and care. Drawing from her immediate surroundings, Masingas work transforms ordinary views into spaces of stillness and connection.

item.title: Eba Morka
item.description: Eba Morka (b. 1999, Ethiopia) is a contemporary printmaker whose practice bridges traditional Ethiopian visual culture with innovative approaches to contemporary printmaking. A graduate of Addis Ababa University's Alle School of Fine Arts and Design, where he completed a Bachelor of Fine Arts in 2025, Morka explores themes of identity, memory, and cultural continuity through layered, richly textured compositions. Drawing inspiration from Ethiopian motifs, symbolism, and material traditions, he combines established printmaking techniques with experimental processes to create works that are both visually intricate and conceptually engaging. His practice reflects on the relationship between personal experience and collective heritage, transforming cultural references into introspective narratives that invite viewers to consider the enduring resonance of history, place, and identity within contemporary life.

item.title: Emmanuel Koto
item.description: Emmanuel Koto (b. 1989, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo) is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans photography, video, sculpture, and installation. Working from an embodied, self-taught methodology, his work investigates the politics of perception: how identities are constructed, negotiated, and often confined through the gaze of others. Drawing from the complexities of racial, social, and cultural hybridity, Koto transforms personal and collective experience into visual inquiries that challenge dominant narratives.His early photo series Kin TV, in which he photographed television broadcasts, evolved into a broader research on societal tensions in contemporary Congolese life. A pivotal moment in his trajectory came in 2019 during a creative exchange in Kinshasa, where he began confronting the psychic weight of visibility and difference, an exploration that continues to define his practice.Kotos work has been exhibited internationally, including: Vantage Point Sharjah 7 (UAE); the Congo Biennale and Lubumbashi Biennale (DRC); Chroniques Urbaines at the Cité de lArchitecture (Paris); and multiple OFF exhibitions of DakArt  Biennale of Contemporary African Art (Senegal). His first institutional solo exhibition took place in 2023 at Horner Eck in Bremen, Germany, following a cross-continental residency between Kinshasa and Bremen.He currently lives and works in Kinshasa, continuing to expand a practice rooted in critical reflection, experimentation, and material transformation.

item.title: Fasil Seboka
item.description: Fasil Seboka (b. 2000, Ethiopia) is a contemporary painter based in Addis Ababa whose practice centres on semi-abstract figurative painting. A graduate of Addis Ababa University's Alle School of Fine Arts and Design, where he completed a Bachelor of Fine Arts in 2025, Seboka combines expressive mark-making with layered compositions to investigate themes of memory, identity, and human connection. Working primarily in oil paint, he balances gestural abstraction with recognisable forms, creating emotionally resonant works that reflect both personal experience and broader social narratives. His paintings are characterised by dynamic brushwork, rich textures, and an intuitive approach to colour, inviting viewers to engage with the fluid relationship between figure and space. Through his evolving practice, Seboka explores the complexities of contemporary life, using painting as a means of expressing the emotional and psychological dimensions of the human experience.

item.title: Gina-Rose Bolligello
item.description: Born in Cape Town, South Africa, in 2001, Gina-Rose Bolligello graduated with a BFA from the University of Cape Towns Michaelis School of Fine Art in 2024. She was awarded both the Simon Gerson Prize and the Directors Award for her final body of work.Her current practice is centered around hauntology and the colonial histories that surround the Cape, highlighting untold historical narratives as a means to educate audiences and keep the memory and work of colonised people alive. In areas where there is a lack of visual documentation, she uses ghosts to narrate and imagine the lives that once were and which are perhaps still present in alternative forms. Her practice explores various media, including photography, video, and printmaking.

item.title: Hauwa Eeyman Mamman
item.description: Hauwa Eeyman Mamman is a Nigerian photographer, known for her work and for participating in portfolio reviews and conversations about her art. She is often referred to as "Eeyman" on social media platforms like Instagram, where she shares her photographic work.

item.title: Itumeleng Mtshali
item.description: Itumeleng Mtshali is a South African contemporary artist whose work explores themes of identity, heritage, and resilience. Through expressive techniques and striking visual language, Mtshali creates pieces that resonate with cultural depth and modern relevance.

item.title: Jacob van Schalkwyk
item.description: Jacob van Schalkwyk (b. 1979, Cape Town) holds a BFA in Drawing from the Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, New York and a MAVA in Sculpture from the University of Stellenbosch, South Africa.His career incorporating painting, drawing, performance, installation and writing has taken his work to the REDCAT Theater in Los Angeles, The Detroit Institute of the Arts, MassMoCA, the BAM Next Wave Festival, Central Park Summerstage, Irving Plaza, The Standard Bank National Arts Festival, The Centre for the Less Good Idea in Johannesburg, De Singel Arts Centre in Antwerp, The Briggait Gallery in Glasgow, The Edinburgh International Fashion Festival and the Salle Jacques Brell in Paris. His visual art has been included in the Neuberg Museum Collection, NY, the König Buro in Zurich, the South African Reserve Bank collection and the Nando’s/Hollard/Spier collections. The Alibi Club, his 2014 debut novel, was published in both Afrikaans and English versions by Umuzi/Random House to critical acclaim.He taught Drawing and Painting at Stellenbosch University between 2016 and 2024, briefly serving as Head of the Fine Arts Department. Van Schalkwyk is a PhD candidate at the University of Pretoria, where he is the recipient of the UP Postgraduate Research Grant. His practice-led research engages with new knowledge obtained from archive detailing significant African contributions to the conceptual basis of gestural abstraction in 1940’s New York City. Van Schalkwyk has been represented by GALLERY AOP and David Krut Projects in Johannesburg and Suburbia Contemporary gallery in Barcelona.

item.title: Jasirah Sayed
item.description: Jasirah Sayed is a fine artist working in printmaking and photography, exploring themes of space, home, and identity. Rooted in personal experience, her practice reflects on how physical and emotional environments shape belonging, particularly through the lens of a young woman growing up in the Western world.Her series Thresholds of Being: Between Home and Horizon examines home as both a physical and emotional landscape shaped by memory, transformation, and renewal. Inspired by the geometry of the Charbagh, the traditional Persian garden, the prints layer collaged photographs and geometric forms to mirror lifes cyclical rhythms. Through this work, Sayed reimagines home as a shifting archive of experience  an evolving threshold between self, place, and possibility.

item.title: Jeannette Unite
item.description: Jeannette Unite is a visual artist who is immersed in the materiality of the art making process whether it is using her own large hand-made chalk-based pastels with mineral oxides or using similar metal oxides in glass artworks, paintings or prints. She uses images, information and metaphors from mining as a point of departure for her reflections on her own personal journeys. She travels to mining and industrial sites for samples, to research and photographically record evidence of the residual remains of power, industrialisation and neo-colonialism on the African landscape. She studied towards a BA Fine Art at the Michaelis School of Art, University of Cape Town from 1981 until 1986, and studied further at UNISA while teaching at Frank Joubert Art Centre until demand for her artwork propelled her into full time art practice in 1997. She continues to live and work in, and travel from her studio in Cape Town.

item.title: Joao Ladeira
item.description: João Ladeira is a contemporary artist whose practice explores themes of migration, displacement, and identity within the context of Africas socio-political and economic realities. Through expressive compositions that blend drawing, painting, and collage, Ladeira humanizes the experiences of migrants and refugees, reflecting on the tragedies and resilience of those crossing the Mediterranean in search of safety.His use of African batiks within postcolonial narratives reclaims symbols of trade and colonialism as emblems of cultural pride and renewal. Engaging with the complexities of globalization, history, and representation, Ladeiras work serves as both a memorial and a call for empathygiving face to the faceless and voice to the voiceless.

item.title: Kelly Fortuin
item.description: Kelly Fortuin is a South African artist and designer from Tafelsig, Mitchells Plain. Working across photography, collage, and digital manipulation, her practice explores memory, place, and belonging, transforming familiar landscapes into layered, vibrant, and unsettled reflections of home.Fortuins work reinterprets ordinary suburban scenes, layering colour and texture to evoke the shifting nature of memory, identity, and community. Trained at Cedar Secondary High School of Arts, Spier Arts Academy (mosaic apprenticeship, Cum Laude, 2019), and the School of Explorative Architecture, she combines artistic and architectural approaches to explore urban landscapes, techno-pastoralism, and hybrid methodologies blending hand drawing with digital rendering.

item.title: Kieron Jina
item.description: Kieron Jina is a multidisciplinary artist, performance maker, and cultural provocateur whose work spans live art, visual collage, and sound. Rooted in performance and ritual, Jina explores belonging, identity, and power through questions of place  shifting focus from Where are you from? to Where do you belong? Their practice weaves Afrofuturism, queer identity, migration, and Indigenous knowledge into immersive, sensory experiences that blur boundaries between body and environment.Holding masters degrees from Wits University and the Academy of Fine Arts Nuremberg, Jinas work resonates with ancestral memory and radical imagination, cultivating spaces for connection, transformation, and liberation.

item.title: Kimberly Bednall
item.description: Kimberley Bednall, born in Cape Town, studied Interior Design at CPUT before pursuing Set Design at RADA in London. Returning home, she continues to draw inspiration from the vibrancy of South Africa and the beauty of Cape Towns landscapes.While earlier works explored the shifting hues of the coastline, her current series turns inland, capturing the rocky hills and delicate resilience of fynbos. Working with charcoal and chalk pastel on 300gsm paper, each piece is mounted over neutral linen with a shadow gap and framed in a white bevelled box, emphasising texture, movement, and a profound sense of place.

item.title: Kimshay Philander
item.description: Kimshay Philander is an early-career visual artist whose practice centres on storytelling through layered meanings and emotional depth. Working across traditional and mixed media, photography remains her primary medium, allowing her to capture the intangible and transform it into visual narrative.Her work explores how geographical places become repositories of human experience, examining home as both a quiet witness to personal memory and a dynamic site of shared histories. Through images of parks, alleyways, and everyday spaces, Philander reflects on the ways environments shape identity, memory, and belonging.

item.title: Kpingni Maureen Douabou
item.description: Kpingni Maureen (1990, Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire) is a visual artist, writer and curator found between the city center of Abidjan, the outskirts of Paris and other territories that fuel her practice. She draws on her Ivorian heritage and the legacy of black feminist thinkers and artists from Africa and its diaspora to shed light on the past, give birth to alternative narratives, question culture and weave new dialogues.Through figurative representations block womens bodies -often her own- Kpingni Maureen seeks to highlight the multiple layers of black femininity across geographies and realities. She understands eroticism and sensuality as spiritual power and a tool for healing, and she explores depiction of the body as a powerful site of resistance, remembrance, pleasure, and transformation. Kpingni-Maureen is a multi-faceted, self-taught cultural practitioner.She expands her visual narratives into interdisciplinary realms, weaving together stories of collective memory, recovery, and the importance of community. Her practice of storytelling also takes the form of a monthly newsletter and a multilingual collaborative pan-African magazine on arts and culture.She has exhibited her work and participated in culural mediation programmes in the United States, France, Côte dIvoire and Ghana. She is a recipient of the 2025 Prince Claus Seed award.

item.title: Kyle Glendinning
item.description: Kyle Glendinning is a Cape Town-based artist whose practice examines the intersection of engineering, architecture, and human ambition. Focusing on engineered vulnerability, he creates intricate paper and mixed-media sculptures that explore how iconic infrastructure both connects communities and embodies fragility.His work, including The Expanse  a 1,640mm paper model of the Millau Viaduct  reinterprets monumental structures to highlight their precariousness, using precision paper engineering alongside wood, thread, steel, and other materials. Through these detailed constructions, Glendinning investigates how physical structures shape collective memory, place, and our understanding of human achievement.

item.title: Lamont Khoza
item.description: Lamont Khoza is a self-taught documentary photographer whose work explores Black working-class life through intimate portraiture. Working primarily with 35mm and 120mm film, Khoza handprints his photographs and experiments with a co-creation technique  allowing his subjects to press the shutter themselves  to challenge ideas of authorship and representation.Influenced by Dawoud Bey, Cherono Ngok, and Roy DeCarava, he seeks to capture dignity, empathy, and authenticity within his community. Since moving to Cape Town in 2022, Khozas images have been featured in PhotoVogues Best Selection of the Month, and he continues to refine his darkroom practice.

item.title: Lona Ndzimande
item.description: Lona Ndzimandes practice explores Black womanhood through the lens of her Zulu upbringing. Using mixed media  including acrylic, Zulu glass beads, fabric, pearls, papier mâché, and paper collage  she creates layered portraits that celebrate Blackness, femininity, and self-expression while interrogating societal expectations and purity culture.Ndzimandes work balances intimacy, defiance, and joy, incorporating textures, draped beads, and sculptural elements to highlight resilience, sensuality, and the complexity of identity. Through her bold visual language, she builds archives of Black femininity that honour tradition while engaging critically with contemporary life.

item.title: Lungiswa Gqunta
item.description: Lungiswa Gqunta (b. 1990, Gqeberha, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary artist working across performance, printmaking, sculpture, and installation. Her practice interrogates spatial exclusion, land ownership, and the lingering legacies of colonialism and patriarchy. Through everyday materials charged with political and social meaning, Gqunta reclaims space and challenges systemic inequalities rooted in race, class, labour, and gender.

item.title: Mahilet Afework
item.description: Mahilet Afework is a painter whose work explores memory, childhood, and emotional recall. Her series Frozen Moments draws from old family photographs and imagined recollections to build portraits that reflect both safety and distance memories felt more than remembered.Using symbolism, familiar items, and texture Mahilet creates visual spaces that speak to the emotional labor of remembering. Her practice questions how the past lives in us: not only through narrative, but in atmosphere, gesture, and absence.In The Weight of Soft Things, her work reclaims the personal archive as a valid visual language for emotional life.

item.title: Maitemogelo Diphetogo Mphela
item.description: Maitemogelo Diphetogo Mphela works in abstraction and mixed media. Her paintings explore belonging and memory through earthy tones, layered textures, and fragments of text. By embedding affirmations and traces of handwriting, she transforms personal reflection into visual form.Mphelas practice investigates the shifting sense of home as both intimate and transient, using acrylic, oil pastels, and mixed materials on canvas and MDF.Her recent exhibitions and studio collaborations position her among South Africas promising emerging artists, contributing to broader conversations about identity and contemporary abstraction.

item.title: Marco Benz
item.description: Marco Mbenza (b. 1997, South Africa) is a South African-born, Congolese photographer and visual artist based in Johannesburg. After studying at the University of Johannesburg, he began his career in film and media production, developing a strong visual language through directing and editing.His passion for storytelling soon pivoted to music videos, where he began collaborating with friends and quickly carved out a niche that blends bold visuals with authentic African culture. As Marco Benz, he has since built a distinctive brand across music videos, short documentaries, and experimental film, earning acclaim for vibrant, culturally resonant work that bridges continents. His practice into photography, Mbenza continues to explore identity, culture, and belonging through a cinematic lens, capturing the energy and emotion of contemporary African life.

item.title: MBadger
item.description: MBadger (b.1992) is a Ghanaian artist whose practice revolves around mythology, surrealism, and bold visual language as a means of communicating personal narrative. Drawing on a background in fashion and illustration, their work transforms intimate experiences into dreamscapes that explore identity, trauma, and transformation.Their education and professional experience span a BFA in Fashion Design from Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD Atlanta) and collaborations with Vivienne Westwood, Studio 189, and Pat McGrath. MBadger’s debut solo exhibition In Relation to Light (2023) explored themes of limitation and self-discovery through the interplay of light and shadow, followed by participation in Echoes of Ghana (2023) and Take Your Place, Beloved (2024). Working across both traditional and digital media, MBadger crafts spaces where the bounds of reality are broken and reimagined, inviting vulnerability, healing, and renewal.

item.title: Mbulelo Terrence Lokoto
item.description: Mbulelo Terrence Lokoto is a South African visual artist working across painting, drawing, and printmaking. His figurative works draw from childhood stories, blending themes of identity, desire, and cultural heritage. Influenced by both traditional values and Pantsula street culture, Lokoto explores the intersection between the spiritual and lived worlds through warm, symbolic compositions that lean toward magical surrealism and realism.

item.title: Milani Mtshotshisa
item.description: Milani Mtshotshisa is a South African visual storyteller whose practice spans photography, fashion, and community-focused work. Born and raised in the Eastern Cape, Mtshotshisa approaches the camera as both an artistic tool and a means of service, preserving memory, dignity, and the everyday realities that shape her community.Her work captures moments of quiet power  steaming pots, children at play, and landscapes framed through intimate perspectives  highlighting culture, survival, and belonging. Trained at the Durban University of Technology (National Diploma in Photography) and AFDA (Higher Certificate in Film, Entertainment, and Television), Mtshotshisa uses photography as a form of healing and dialogue, affirming resilience and giving voice to the often unseen.

item.title: Mwamba Chikwemba
item.description: Mwamba Chikwemba born in Kitwe, Zambia in 1992 lives in Lusaka, Zambia. Coming from a Public Administration and IT background, Mwamba is a trained artists from the Schooling of the Council of Visual Artists in Zambia. She describes herself as a painter, street artist and print maker drawing inspiration from a combination of art movements like portrait and figurative art. Mwamba is influenced by artists like Geoffrey Phiri, Daut Makala, Agness Buya Yombwe, Frida Kahlo, Jenny Saville and Wycliffe Mundopa.In June 2016 she was selected as the artist of the year under German Embassy Lusaka, taking part in a number of local workshops on printmaking and painting. She has done several public murals in Lusaka, Livingstone, Kampala, Antananarivo to Johannesburg. Mwamba has also gone through schools of learning and residency at Modzi Arts (Zambia), Nafasi Art Space (Tanzania), Isart Galerie (Madagascar) and Great More Studio (South Africa). She has been awarded the Push Women Award, winner of the Cynthia Zukas young artist award and been granted the Summer academy of fine arts in Austria, Salzburg on relief Printing and Pronto Plate Lithography.

item.title: Myra Brown
item.description: Myra Brown is a Cape Townbased photographic artist whose work explores intimacy, identity, and place through traditional darkroom techniques. Her series Opaque Clarity reflects on queer relationships and the emotional charge of everyday spaces, captured in a deadpan yet tender style. Rooted in observation since childhood, Browns images reveal vulnerability, joy, and resilience as a trans woman navigating lifes shifting landscapes.A 2022 graduate of the Cape Town School of Photography, she continues to refine a quiet visual language that transforms personal experience into universal reflection.

item.title: Nerissa Brobbey
item.description: Nerissa Brobbey was born in Accra, Ghana to Ghanaian and Romanian parents. Nerissa started painting at the age of three years old when her father noticed her drawing constantly with the paper from his typewriter. She was the youngest art student enrolled at the Children's Club in Bucharest, Romania and, under the mentorship of Romanian artist Mariana Palea, she began painting in oil on canvas at the age of five.She has had exhibitions in Romania, Ghana and USA as a child and as a marketing student. Most recently she has exhibited at Nubuke Gallery (Accra, Ghana) and The World Bank Offices (Accra, Ghana).Nerissa studied Economics and French at Bates College, Maine, USA and International Marketing at Hult International Business School in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA. While at Bates, she studied abroad in France, Scotland, Hungary, Turkey and the Czech Republic and during this time she also traveled to Canada, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Ireland, Spain, Belgium and Austria.She has continued to paint as a hobby. Upon the last count, there are about 400 works of art made by her at her residence.

item.title: Ngollo Mlengeya
item.description: Ngollo Mlengeya is a visual artist based in Arusha,Tanzania. Working primarily with mixed media, she creates textured artworks that draw inspiration from the rich tapestry of everyday life.Through her practice, Mlengeya seeks to explore the grand meanings that underlie our quotidian experiences. By incorporating diverse materials and techniques into her pieces, she crafts visually striking compositions that reflect the complexity and beauty of the human condition.Born and raised in Tanzania ,Mlengeyas unique perspective is informed by her lived experiences in Tanzania. Yet her themes of connection, identity, and the search for meaning resonate with audiences from all walks of life. Through her multifaceted practice, she encourages a greater appreciation for the transformative power of art to illuminate the extraordinary within the ordinary.Ngollo mlengeyas pieces can be found in private collections around the world. As she continues to push the boundaries of her medium, Mlengeya remains dedicated to creating art that celebrates the richness and complexity of the human experience.

item.title: Nic Human
item.description: Natasha Carstens is a South African artist whose recent body of work forms part of her PhD research at Durban University of Technology. Her paintings engage with the Anthropocene debate, positioning art within the broader ecological discourse. The series features nine large-scale depictions of sea turtles along the KwaZulu-Natal coast, exploring themes of environmental impact, resilience, and interconnectedness. Her artworks are available for purchase on Latitudes Online.

item.title: N’cho Jean-Louis
item.description: Jean-Louis Ncho is an Ivorian photographer whose practice bridges fine art, street, and conceptual photography.His work explores identity, memory, and heritage through series such as Les Abidjanais and Mondoukou, which combine street scenes with Akan and Adinkra symbols. Initially photographing with his phone, he developed a distinctive style that celebrates Africas visual languages.A recipient of the 2024 Prazzle Galaxy Grant, Ncho has exhibited at the African Foto Fair, Yaoundé Photo Fest, and Kampala Foto Lubumbashi.

item.title: Ololade Lawal
item.description: Based in Lagos, Nigeria, Oloade Lawal is a visual artist who inquires' through lens-based mediums, abstract paintings and currently exploring an interdisciplinary practice. Her works mostly are personalized commentary on detachment, with situational evidence based on her lived experiences.She studied Mass Communication at Yaba College of Technology. She has participated in both group exhibitions and Art fairs. She had her first solo show in 2023 and she features in Ake Review that same year. She is a Kuta Arts Residency Alumna and was recently a partiipant at G.A.S foundation Imora Arts Intensive Fellowship.

item.title: Pako Lesejane
item.description: Pako Lesejane is a Botswana-based landscape and fine art photographer whose practice bridges the natural world with experimental artistic processes. Educated at the National College of Photography in Pretoria and further refined through mentorship at the Martin Osner Gallery in Cape Town, Lesejane brings together technical mastery and an insatiable curiosity for creative exploration.A passionate traveler and adventurer, Lesejane draws inspiration from the diverse terrains he encounters—transforming these journeys into visual narratives that evoke emotion rather than mere documentation. Over time, his artistic vision has evolved toward fine art photography: a discipline that resists immediacy and rewards the patience of slow, deliberate creation.Lesejane’s practice transcends traditional photography. His works often begin as photographic prints, which he then transforms through layered interventions—using acrylics, watercolor, sugar overlays, and unconventional chemical substances. His acclaimed piece Rugose Baobab, for instance, achieves its distinctive texture through an experimental treatment with household detergent. At times, he may burn, tear, or chemically alter his prints—each gesture an act of artistic inquiry and transformation.“For me, fine art photography is not about capturing what the camera sees,” Lesejane explains, “but about rendering what the artist envisions.” His approach invites the viewer to engage with texture, feeling, and interpretation, rather than simply observing a scene. Influenced by the philosophies of pioneering photographers, he embraces a creative freedom that privileges intuition and experimentation over rigid technique.In some of his compositions, Lesejane employs tools such as Neutral Density filters to manipulate light and motion, guiding the viewer’s eye with intention and precision. The resulting images challenge perception, expanding the possibilities of what photography can be and positioning him as a distinctive voice within Botswana’s contemporary art landscape.Through his work, Pako Lesejane offers more than images—he shares emotions, processes, and stories. Each piece becomes an invitation to enter a layered, tactile world where photography merges with painting, alchemy, and the imaginative spirit of art itself.

item.title: Palesa Motheo
item.description: Palesa Motheo is a multimedia artist working in sculpture and painting whose practice draws on Sotho and Matebele heritage. She explores cultural memory, the matriarchive, and the intersections of tradition and modernity in post-colonial Southern Africa, investigating how histories are archived, erased, and reimagined.Her work engages with locality as a living archive, examining how streets, homes, and landscapes carry ancestral memory alongside contemporary negotiations of identity and belonging. Working in wood, stone, paint, and mixed media, Motheo creates sculptural and wall-based works that reference domestic and ritual objects, holding space for the interweaving of heritage, memory, and environment.

item.title: Quinton Mawila
item.description: Born in Limpopo and raised in Gauteng, Quinton Mawila is a multidisciplinary artist working across photography and cinematography. His work explores individuality, healing, and the human experience, examining how identity is shaped through the body, memory, and lived experience. Through his lens, Mawila redefines vulnerability and strength as interconnected, creating visual narratives that celebrate humanity in all its diversity. He has exhibited with BCX, Kameraz at Open Window, and in group shows at the Open Window Institute.As an emerging artist, he continues to expand the language of lens-based storytelling, using his art as a meditative space for reflection, connection, and transformation.

item.title: Ribka Sisay
item.description: Ribka Sisay is a self-taught photographer and mixed-media artist whose practice grew out of a period of deep personal rupture. Originally a writer, she turned to photography during a time when depression made words feel unreachable. Through self-portraiture, weaving, and hand-stitching, Ribka began reconstructing her inner worldone image at a time.Her current body of work involves woven self-portraits, photographic prints that are physically cut, threaded, and sewn together. The result is both vulnerable and intricate: layered compositions that reflect a self in transition, fragmented but reassembling. Influenced by craft traditions and emotional survival, Ribka uses tactile processes to explore identity, isolation, and healing. In The Weight of Soft Things, her work becomes a kind of visual journaling, intimate and process-driven, inviting viewers to witness the often-invisible work of becoming whole.

item.title: Roanna Tella
item.description: With each brushstroke, Roanna Tella maps the shifting terrain between emotion and memory, vulnerability and resilience. Rooted in introspection, her practice reimagines the human form through gestural abstraction, inviting us to witness how the body can carry both rest and rupture.In her newest body of work, Foreboding Tales, Roanna turns inward, tracing the delicate rituals that tether us to joy and grounding, even in the midst of uncertainty. Through the symbolism of plants and quiet daily gestures, she asks: how we hold beauty and distress in the same breath?Roanna holds a B.A in Visual Arts from the University of Lagos and has exhibited widely across Nigeria and internationally. Her evolving practice continues to deepen through mentorship and a commitment to emotional truth in visual form.

item.title: Rosalie Boka
item.description: Boka Amenan Rosalie was born in 1997, in Ouellé, Côte dIvoire. Her early discovery of her artistic talent led her to enroll in a high school for art training, and after graduating , she entered the Ecole Nationale des Beaux-Arts d'Abidjan, where she had the opportunity to benefit from the knowledge of several Ivorian masters and contemporary artists. Above all, she discovered her unconditional love for painting.Rosalie's works lie at the crossroads of dreams and memories, where roots become veins, and foliage becomes skies hiding timeless stories. By combining vibrant textures, dreamlike palettes, and organic forms, each painting transports us to a universe where nature becomes a living theater, inhabited by presences that are both familiar and elusive.

item.title: Ruth Getachew
item.description: Ruth Getachew is a collage and mixed-media artist whose work explores the emotional and energetic imprints we carry. A graduate of the Alle School of Fine Arts and Design, her practice is shaped by personal experiences with emotional burnout and a deep interest in quantum theory and vibrational healing.In her series, Ruth uses abstraction, color, and texture to reflect on how memory, media, and environment shape internal states. Her works function as emotional maps urging viewers to reflect on what they absorb and emit daily. In this exhibition, her collages challenge the notion that emotional life is peripheral, insisting instead that it forms the foundation of how we live.

item.title: Shadai Moonsamy
item.description: Shadai Moonsamy is a South African contemporary visual artist based in Durban. Her multidisciplinary practice spans painting, printmaking, and mixed media, exploring identity, memory and urban life through layered textures and expressive forms.

item.title: Sheila Bayley
item.description: Sheila Bayley (b. 1986, Nairobi) was raised in a culturally diverse environment that continues to shape her artistic practice. Holding a Bachelors degree in Psychology from the United States International UniversityAfrica, she is a self-taught artist whose work explores themes of identity, urbanization, and the delicate balance between nature and nurture in shaping human behavior.Working primarily with acrylic and paper collage on canvasand on paper for her smaller piecesSheila draws inspiration from memory, personal experience, and poetry to create evocative compositions that invite viewers on an introspective journey of thought and emotion.In 2021, she was the guest artist at the Kobo Open Studio Art Sale & Exhibition in Nairobi. Two years later, she presented her first solo exhibition at Peponi Hotel in Lamu, followed by her first international duo show at Gallery Brulhart in Geneva, Switzerland. She has also participated twice in the Affordable Art Fair organized by the National Museum Society of Kenya. Her artworks are held in private collections locally and internationally, including in Zanzibar, the United States, France, the UAE, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Switzerland.Sheila is deeply committed to the growth and development of the East African art scene and envisions establishing an educational system that positions art as both a life skill and a viable career path. As her practice continues to evolve, she remains open to local and international collaborations, residencies, and exhibition opportunities.

item.title: Simphiwe Fuwe Molefe
item.description: Simphiwe Fuwe Molefe (b. 1990, Nquthu, KwaZulu-Natal) is a documentary and narrative photographer based in Katlehong, South Africa. He joined the Of Soul and Joy photography programme in 2019, where he was introduced to photography as a tool for storytelling and social reflection.Molefes work has since been widely exhibited as he recently presented his project Ungowakwethu wena in a group exhibition at the JSE,. In 2025, his photographs were featured in I Put My Hand on My Chest to Feel My Heartbeat at Constitution Hill, a milestone that led to coverage in the Mail & Guardian. In 2024, he exhibited at the Joburg FNB Art Fair.In 2023, he was named Global Citizens Emerging Creative of the Month, and he is also the recipient of the 17th Tierney Fellowship, one of South Africas most respected photography awards.His projects have appeared in numerous group exhibitions, including Through the Lens Collective (portrait exhibition), Uhambo at Umhlabathi Gallery, and in the Of Soul and Joy tenthanniversary book, where his project Dikarabo was published alongside the work of nine other South African photographers. A graduate of the Market Photo Workshops Advanced Photography Programme, Molefe continues to build a distinct voice within contemporary South African photography, exploring themes of identity, community, and lived experience.

item.title: Simphiwe Ndzube
item.description: Simphiwe Ndzube (b. 1990, Johannesburg, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans painting, collage, performance, and sculpture. His vivid, surreal worlds explore freedom, transformation, and the lingering effects of post-apartheid South Africa. Drawing from mythology, history, and storytelling, Ndzube reimagines narratives of identity and power through dynamic figures and landscapes. He lives and works between Los Angeles and Cape Town.

item.title: Stella Ekpe Samuel
item.description: Stella Ekpe Samuel is a multtidisciplinary artist based in Lagos, Nigeria. She holds a degree in Fine Arts and Design from the University of Port Harcourt, with a focus in painting. Her work explores themes of identity, womanhood, memory and personal storytelling, often using her own image as a central subject.Known for her rich textures and layered surfaces, Stella works with materials like paper, broken glass, and fabric to create emotionally charged, tactile paintings. Through personal experimentation, she develoed a unique texturing technique using paper, layering and maipulating it to create ripplie like effects that echo waves of thought and feeling.Her art reflects both quiet introspection nd cultural depth, drawing inspiration from everyday life and artists like Njideka Akunyili Crosby and Frida Kahlo. Stella has exhibited in several group shows, inculding October Rain at Gemini Gallery (2023), Artist Commune ot OneArtt Gallery (2024), and Plus234Art Fair in collaboration with Soto Gallery (2025). Her practice continues to evolve as she explores new ways to tell stories through material, form and emotion.

item.title: Sundus Saad
item.description: Sundus Saad is a Cape Town-based South African-Arab fibre artist specialising in on- and off-loom weaving. Her work explores life, relationships, and interconnectedness, using yarns of varied textures and colours  often green, symbolising peace and prosperity.Guided by intuition and energy, Saad creates organically in states of calm, producing works meant to be shared and appreciated while remaining a personal practice of fulfilment.

item.title: Tesfahun Kibru
item.description: Tesfahun Kibru, (b.1970) is a 2000 sculpture graduate of the Alle School of Fine Arts and Design, is a dedicated artist committed to a philosophy of complete immersion in art. Rejecting the ordinary, Kibru has consistently sought to express his unique artistic vision and individuality across all aspects of his life, resulting in a versatile and adaptable approach to creative challenges.For the past two decades, Kibru has worked as a full-time studio artist, transforming experience into wisdom and nurturing self-confidence as both a person and an artist. He has cultivated a distinct voice in contemporary Ethiopian art, marked by numerous solo and group exhibitions. A pivotal relationship with Asni Art Gallery served as a launching pad for his career, where he gained valuable exposure through solo shows, group exhibitions, and an artist residency.

item.title: Thando Salman
item.description: Thando Salman (b. 1997, Johannesburg) is a multidisciplinary artist based in Kempton Park. His work explores the lived realities of Black youth in South Africa, particularly young men, through themes of identity and contemporary existence. A Fine Arts graduate from the University of the Witwatersrand and recipient of the Anya Millman Scholarship for Artistic Excellence, Salman also received the 2021 SAFFCA Entabeni Residency. He has exhibited locally and internationally, including at FNB Art Fair, Latitudes Art Fair (solo with BKhz Gallery), and UTA Artist Space in Atlanta.

item.title: Theresia
item.description: ,p>Theresia is a self-taught emerging artist from Tanzania whose expressive paintings draw inspiration from everyday life, African traditions, and personal experience. Her passion for art began in childhood, influenced by cartoons and local newspaper illustrations, and was reignited during her medical training amid the COVID-19 lockdown. Working primarily with acrylicswhile also exploring oil pastels, charcoal, and graphiteTheresias art celebrates beauty, emotion, and colour.Influenced by Jean-Michel Basquiat and Henri Matisse, she experiments with diverse styles to create vibrant, reflective works. She has exhibited widely, including at Rangi Gallery, Nafasi Art Space, and DARCH (Old Boma), where she held her first solo show in 2023.

item.title: Turakella Editha Gyindo (Tura)
item.description: Turakella Editha Leonard Gyindo (Tura) is a Tanzanian artist and curator whose multidisciplinary practice spans painting, performance, video, and installation. Her work examines human adaptability in a rapidly changing world, challenging colonial and societal constructs around identity, intersectionality, and belonging. With a background in Chemical and Processing Engineering from Université de Badji Mokhtar in Algeria, Tura transitioned into the arts and completed the Curatorial Practices and Art Management Program at Nafasi Art Space Academy in 2021.She later founded Deja Vu Studios, an experimental platform for artistic research and collaboration. Her work has been featured in the East Africa Biennale (2021), FNB Art Joburg, and a solo exhibition at Alliance Française in Dar es Salaam (2024).

item.title: Valerie Asiimwe Amani
item.description: Valerie Asiimwe Amani is a Tanzanian artist and writer whose anti-disciplinary practice investigates the relationship between body, language, and myth; exploring how they shape belonging, memory, and collective imagination.Drawing from personal contemporary experiences, feminist theory, and spiritual ecologies, Amani explores the permeable boundaries between the political, domestic, and intimate. She has exhibited internationally, with presentations in Lagos, New York, Paris, Cape Town, London, Leipzig, Zanzibar, and Dar es Salaam. Recent exhibitions include Immortal Apples, Eternal Eggs at Hastings Contemporary and Amani: Kukita Kungoa at Museen Stade, Germany.She is the 2023 Foundwork Art Prize Honouree and a 2022 Ingram Prize winner. Her work has appeared in Art Monthly, Hyperallergic, and Texte zur Kunst. Amani is currently based in Oxford, where she is pursuing a practice-led DPhil in Fine Art at The Ruskin School of Art, University of Oxford.

item.title: Van Andréa
item.description: Van Andréa is a Congolese (Congo-Brazzaville) painter and sculptor. He graduated from the Ecole Nationale des Beaux-Arts in Brazzaville, where for his final examination he presented works based on the world of the "sapeurs" from his Bacongo neighborhood.These pieces, made with papier-mâché on canvas and as sculptures, were titled "Sape Art and the Sapeurs of Brazzaville." This led to his first national solo exhibition at Ateliers Sahm in 2013, titled "Smoke Without Fire." A year later, he won first prize at the second edition of RIAC in Brazzaville, earning him a creative residency at the Blachère Foundation in France. His first international solo exhibition took place in Switzerland, at Gasteateliers Krone Aarau in 2015. Beginning in 2019, Van Andréa began revisiting masterpieces from the Italian Renaissance, reinterpreting them based on the inspiration each one evoked. From Caravaggio’s "The Cardsharps," retitled "Damoiseau," to Lucien Melingue’s "The Provost of Merchants Étienne Marcel and the Dauphin Charles," renamed "The Bourgeoises," his new collection, titled "Renaissance," explores the theme: Corruption of Morals. The use of Ankara fabric for the headscarves of his female figures remains his artistic signature. These women, with their carefully tied headwraps, reflect the artist’s admiration for his grandmother. Van Andréa has emerged through a remarkable journey that can be summarized as follows: Initially introduced to the Congolese public at Ateliers Sahm in 2013 with a solo exhibition, he went on to win the second edition of the International Contemporary Art Meeting (RIAC), which led to his participation in the Dakar Biennale in Senegal in 2014.

item.title: Vita Malulu
item.description: Vita Malulu, born in Kabila village, Magu district, Mwanza, Tanzania, is a multidisciplinary artist working in painting, sculpture, and ceramics. From childhood, he was inspired by his surroundings and the expressive sketches of a local mute herder, which sparked his lifelong passion for visual storytelling. After training at Bagamoyo College of Arts (TASUBA, 20032006) and engaging with artist collectives such as Nafasi Art Space and 14+ Artists, Malulu has developed a practice that blends traditional techniques with experimental forms, often using recycled and found materials. His work interrogates social and political realities, highlighting the struggles and resilience of marginalized communities in Tanzania and beyond. Malulus art is both a reflection of personal memory and a dialogue with broader society.Through painting, sculpture, and music, he explores themes of inequality, labor, and the human experience, creating works that resonate locally and internationally. His exhibitions and residencies across Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Sweden, and Norway have further shaped his vision of art as a transformative and communal practice. Today, he continues to produce work that challenges, provokes, and inspires, using creativity to give voice to those often overlooked while fostering engagement and reflection through his installations and performances.

item.title: Waleed Mohammed
item.description: Waleed Mohammed (Wamo) (b. 2000, Khartoum, Sudan) is a Sudanese visual artist based in Nairobi, Kenya. His work explores memory, migration, and identity through reimagined archival photographs and layered materiality. Deeply influenced by Sudanese heritage and the evolving narratives of displacement, Waleed’s practice engages with vintage studio portraits and photographs from the 1950s–70s, recontextualizing them through contemporary textures and color palettes to bridge generations and geographies, combines painting, mixed media, and cotton yarns to transform personal and collective memories into a contemporary visual language that questions belonging, absence, and cultural continuity.He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Fine and Applied Arts from Sudan University of Science and Technology. Since his first solo exhibition in 2022 in Khartoum, his work has been presented in various group exhibitions across Sudan, Spain, Germany, Portugal, the United States, Kenya and Egypt. In 2024, he was awarded the MRI Fund for Artists Under Risk by the Goethe-Institut in Nairobi, Waleed works from his studio in Nairobi, where he is also co-founding a Sudanese art collective with fellow artists to foster artistic exchange and community engagement.

item.title: William Joseph Kachinjika
item.description: William Joseph Kachinjika is a Harare-based artist working with textiles and found materials to explore memory, hybridity, and the transformative power of objects. Inspired by childhood lessons in basket weaving from his grandmother, he creates large-format woven pieces from rope, cables, and mutton cloth, bridging indigenous craft and contemporary practice.His series Country Game Game reflects on Zimbabwes power crisis, resilience, and history, drawing on a childhood game that combines geography, culture, and play. Kachinjika trained at the School of Visual Art and Design, National Gallery of Zimbabwe, and continues his practice at Mbare Art Space under mentorship from Moffat Takadiwa and others.

item.title: Emma Thompson
item.description: Emma Thompson is an artist based in Limpopo, South Africa, who creates mixed-media prints and works with etching.

item.title: Emma Wootton
item.description: Emma Wootton (b.2002 South Africa) works, and lives in Cape Town. Her focus on soft sculpture is shaped by her lifelong interest in fibre arts. In 2024 she graduated with distinction from Michaelis School of Fine Art, majoring in sculpture and print making. She was co-awarded the Michaelis Prize in 2024, and the Simon Gerson Prize in Both 2023 and 2024.

item.title: Maphoso George Mokwena
item.description: Maphoso George Mokwena is an emerging visual artist born in 1997 in Lephalale, Limpopo Province, South Africa. He graduated from Tielelo Secondary School in 2017 and was awarded a full bursary to study art by Elegant Fuel in 2020. In 2021, he enrolled at the Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg to study printmaking.Mokwena’s body of work is deeply influenced by his journey between Lephalale & Johannesburg and make people to rethink how we measure worth by honouring both economic struggle and personal triumph rooted in family and resilience.He works with various media, including pen, charcoal, acrylic, digital and oil paint. Mokwena has participated in numerous group exhibitions and was featured in publications such as Art Times, Hyper Blog Magazine and Ntshabele Newspaper. In 2024, Mokwena travelled to Italy to paint 90metre long community memorial mural, in 2025 he completed internship in printmaking at Artist Proof Studio and practice as an artist and printmaker.

item.title: Michaele van den Heever
item.description: Michaele van den Heever is a South African visual artist working primarily in monotype and print-based processes. Her work explores faces, silhouettes, and shadowed forms to navigate presence, absence, and emotional visibility. Drawn to limitation and imperfection, she works by adding and removing ink, allowing erosion, erasure, and restraint to shape each image. Faces without eyes recur in her practice, refusing direct engagement and instead holding tension, quietness, and ambiguity. Through a reduced palette and an intuitive process, her work reflects inner landscapes, mental states, and the subtle marks left by lived experience.

item.title: Misa Boshoma Tinkie
item.description: Misa Boshoma Tinkie is a South African Artist, her art stems from a deeply personal journey and a desire to express the complex emotions of womanhood and social struggle. She explore the expectations placed on women and the silent battles they endure- between self-blame, judgment, and the search for freedom.Working mainly in printmaking, especially cyanotype, monotypes and linocuts, she embrace both control and unpredictability. The process often produces smudges or fading, symbolizing the fragility of emotions and the shifting nature of identity. Her recurring blue floral patterns, inspired by Chinese vase designs, represent how women are often valued like delicate objects-cherished until cracked, when their worth is questioned though their essence remains intact.Through her work, she challenge these perceptions and reclaim the authenticity pf womanhood. She aim to create a space where silenced emotions can be seen, shared, and understood-reflecting both her own experiences and those of countless others.

item.title: Mncedisi Mchunu
item.description: Mncedisi Mchunu is a visual artist from Soweto, Johannesburg. He began his artistic journey at Artist Proof Studio in 2023 and is currently in his third and final year of study. Mchunu is recognised for his distinctive graphic, non-traditional drawing style, primarily realised through printmaking techniques including monotype, drypoint, linocut, and etching.His practice explores themes of mental health, emotional well-being, and personal experience, seeking to articulate the unconscious mind through symbolic and religious imagery. Drawing on intersectional identities, Mchunus work invites viewers to engage both intellectually and emotionally, fostering reflection and connection.

item.title: Moeketsi Motlhabe
item.description: Moeketsi Motlhabe (b. 2003, Centurion, South Africa) is a visual artist currently based in johannesburg. Born and bred in Pretoria, Motihabe developed a deep appreciation for the cultural and historical layers embedded within his surroundings. He completed his secondary education in 2020 and is currently pursuing a Bachelor of fine arts at the University of Johannesburg ,with a primary focus on printmaking. Motihabe's printmaking and drawing practice engages with the complex legacies of colonial architecture in South Africa-structures whose beauty and craftsmanship stand in stark contrast to histories of land dispossession, exploitation, and systemic oppression. Rooted in his identity as a Black South African descendant of the colonized, he navigates the tension between appreciating formal elegance and confronting the violent realities these buildings embody. Through the layered processes inherent to printmaking, reproduction, multiplication, and overlay.

item.title: Nazeerah Jacub
item.description: Visual Artist, Jacub Nazeerah (1993.) born in the heart of Johannesburg spent her early life in a predominantly Muslim community, wherein the pursuit of art was inaccessible and discouraged. Jacub. N, began oil painting from the tender age of fourteen following her passion for painting and graduated with a Visual Art Honours degree from the University of Johannesburg in 2016. Jacub. N, won a merit award from Thami Mnyele and as well as the Sasol New Signatures competition.She has featured in the Emerging Painters show at Turbine Art Fair and was selected top 100 artists to exhibit at the Other Art Fair, Australia. Her artworks are featured on Saatchi Art and she has also exhibited at Pretoria Art Museum along with numerous group-shows in galleries in and around Gauteng, such as Art it is, UJ Gallery, Art Lovers to name a few with a group exhibition at the RMB Think Precinct with the Talent unlocked residency in 2024.Nazeerah is an independent artist, wife and mother of two young girls and runs her studio from Johannesburg. Nazeerah has graduated from International Sculpture-Painting school and is currently working on her new body of work for her upcoming solo show (Un)Natural Bloom in her awarded studio at the Bag Factory in Newtown through the Young Womxn Studio Bursary 2025.Drawing on the preservation of stories passed through generations,(Un)Natural Bloom follows her body of work (Un)Belonging addressing the notion of transcending boundaries across cultural landscapes. (Un)Natural Bloom is an invitation to see how life, experience and memory persist in natural forms that were once fragile and enduring, echoing the tensions of growth in disrupted landscapes and of the resilience of the female blooming under constraint.

item.title: Ndivhuwo Marubini
item.description: Ndivhuwo Marubini was born on 9th April in South Africa. She completed her primary and secondary education at St. Vincent School for the Deaf. In 2023, she enrolled full-time at Artist Proof Studio, where she is currently completing her third year of printmaking. Recently, she received an award for exhibiting her work at the Wits Centre for Deaf Studies Deaf Art and Film Festival.Ndivhuwo looks forward to completing her stu00dies and pursuing a four-year internship at Artist Proof Studio to deepen her experience in printmaking. She aspires to build a successful artistic career both locally and internationally, using her art to inspire and empower others within the Deaf community.

item.title: Noluthando Ntsuntsha
item.description: Noluthando Ntsuntsha (b. 2001, Soweto, Johannesburg) is a South African visual artist and printmaker. She completed her studies at St. Vincent School for the Deaf in 2021 before beginning her artistic journey at Artist Proof Studio in 2023, where she is currently in her third year of study. Ntsuntsha works primarily with printmaking techniques including linocut and drypoint, exploring image-making through material and process.In 2025, she exhibited an earlier artwork at the Deaf Art and Film Festival at Wits Art Park, Parktown. Deeply inspired by her teacher Raymond Fuyana, her practice is shaped by the cultures and lived experiences of Deaf communities in Johannesburg, Soweto, and Newcastle. Newcastles rich history and diversity have had a particularly strong influence on her artistic perspective, informing her engagement with identity, place, and community. Ntsuntsha aspires to complete a fourth-year internship at Artist Proof Studio to further develop her printmaking practice and establish herself as a professional Deaf artist.

item.title: Poloko Mosoeunyane
item.description: Poloko Mosoeunyane is a South African visual artist born in Orange Farm, Gauteng (Vaal). His multidisciplinary practice brings together collage, painting, drawing, original writing, and printmaking processes including drypoint, linocut, silkscreen, and lithography. Through the layering of image, text, and material, Mosoeunyane investigates themes of rights and responsibility, as well as memory and time.His work reflects a thoughtful engagement with social consciousness and personal reflection, using process as a means of examining how histories are constructed, remembered, and carried forward.

item.title: Renneth Mhlongo
item.description: Renneth Hlawutelo Mhlongo was born in Thomo village, located in Giyani, Limpopo. He attended Mashengani Primary School and Hanyani Thono High School, where he honed his skills under the guidance of his art teacher and motivator, Mr. Khosa. Currently, he is practicing printmaking at the Artist Proof Studio, mentored by Kim Berman, Osiah Masukameng, and the late Nhlahla Xaba. He began his studies in 2023 and is now in his third year, training to become a professional printmaker. His work focuses on landscapes and animals, where he combines elements from rural and urban areas to celebrate his roots and current surroundings.

item.title: Simphiwe Dlamini
item.description: Simphiwe Dlamini is a South African printmaker who was born in KwaZulu-Natal and now lives in Johannesburg. Her work often explores themes of memory, loss, and grief, using a recurring pigeon symbol in dreamlike, utopian environments. She utilizes various mediums and techniques, and has exhibited her work, including at the Turbine Art Fair and the Vrystaat Arts Festival.

item.title: Tecla Spiller
item.description: A South African Johannesburg based artist working predominantly in Linocut.

item.title: Thabang Leboa
item.description: Thabang Anthony Leboa is a talented deaf printmaking artist born in 1999 in Kwathema, Johannesburg, South Africa. He attended Ekurhuleni High School for Deaf and Blind Learners, where he cultivated his passion for the arts. Currently, Thabang is in his third year at the Artist Proof Studio, specialising in various print techniques, including linocut, drypoint, and silkscreen. With plans to enrol for his fourth year at the Artist Proof Studio in 2026, Thabang aims to further refine his skills and establish himself as a professional printmaker. He has a unique passion for fashion, focusing on printing designs on clothing. Additionally, Thabang enjoys drawing and painting, allowing him to express his creativity in multiple mediums. His work reflects a blend of personal experience and artistic innovation, making a significant impact in the contemporary art scene.

item.title: Thato S. Nhlapho
item.description: Thato S. Nhlapo (b. 1990, Ratanda, Heidelberg) is a South African visual artist whose practice bridges the raw energy of graffiti with the refinement of traditional fine art. His work is a vivid exploration of urban narratives, cultural memory, and the tension between street expression and the gallery space.

item.title: Tlhalefo Motsemonnye
item.description: My name is Tlhalefo Motsemonnye. I was born in the North West, grew up in Soweto, and currently live in Ekurhuleni, specifically Sky City.I am popularly known as Slice. Graffiti introduced me to the art world, and I am one of the featured painters at Africa's largest Hip Hop festival, which takes place in Newtown, Johannesburg. My artistic journey began with streetwear and then evolved into photography. Graffiti and skateboarding became part of my life as I was nearing the completion of my matriculation.

item.title: Vas Putter
item.description: VAS PUTTER is a differently-abled artist currently residing between KwaZulu Natal and Johannesburg. Her training includes various art disciplines with a focus on Printmaking and Art History. She is fascinated with the diaspora of peoples and the displacement of artefacts. Working in paint mediums, printmaking and assemblage with discarded objects, her work explores humanitarian and environmental issues while at the same time unpacking historical and contemporary influences on her life. Her commissions include the cover of “In the Storms of History – South Africa’s Journey from Slavery to Democracy” (L Grobbelaar 2023), artworks for the National Museum of Bloemfontein (Art Bank SA 2024) and waste-to-art sculptures for the Trade and Industrial Policy Strategies conference (2024). Putter has taken part in various group exhibitions across the country as well as held a solo show at the Alliance Francaise de Pretoria in 2025. In 2024, she has exhibited at The Inaugural Global Artivism Conference (Tshwane). Her project Averting the Gaze, highlighting the links between the global supply chain and neo-slavery, was supported by The National Arts Council. In March 2025 she was a panellist for the National Arts Council 2025 Human Right’s Day Webinar as well as the guest speaker for the opening of The Printing Girls exhibition at the Association of Arts, Pretoria – speaking about fostering community and inclusivity in the arts. In September 2025, she was invited to speak at the annual South African Visual Art Historians conference about the ‘Averting the Gaze’ artworks focussing on humanitarian and environmental practices.

item.title: Aimee Linde
item.description: Aimee Linde began her journey in ceramics just 3.5 years ago. What started as a creative exploration quickly evolved into a serious practice, culminating in the establishment of her own home-based studio. Specialising in hand-built, one-ofa-kind sculptural lamps and interior décor pieces, her work blurs the line between functional design and expressive art.Driven by a deep passion for form, texture, and materiality, she crafts lighting pieces that are not only practical but also boldly artistic – introducing a fresh, seldom-seen aesthetic to the world of interiors. With an eye for detail and a fearless approach to scale and shape, her work is poised to make a strong impact on the design market, offering something truly original to collectors, galleries and interior designers.

item.title: Lesedi
item.description: Lesedi is an artist on Latitudes Online.

item.title: Sitaara Stodel & Zenaéca Singh
item.description: Sitaara Stodel and Zenaéca Singh are South African contemporary artists whose practices intersect through explorations of memory, identity, and the material traces of history.Based in Cape Town, Sitaara Stodel reconstructs personal and collective memories using found family photographs, collage, and printmaking. Her work reflects on home, nostalgia, and belonging, shaped by a childhood marked by constant movement and the search for stability.Zenaéca Singh, a Durban-born artist, examines the legacy of indentured Indian labour and colonial histories in South Africa. Using sugar, molasses, resin, and archival imagery, she creates tactile paintings and sculptures that confront erasure while reimagining cultural identity.Together, their practices offer intimate yet expansive reflections on how personal experience, material memory, and social history intertwineeach piece available for collection on Latitudes Online.

item.title: Warren Maroon
item.description: Warren Maroon (b. 1985) is a Cape Town-based sculptor whose work is deeply rooted in his personal history. Growing up in Mitchell’s Plain on the Cape Flats, an area associated with significant social challenges, Maroon turned to art as a means of escape and a tool for expression. He graduated from Ruth Prowse with a Diploma in Fine Art in 2011, finding his distinct voice as a sculptor in 2018.Inspired by an Arte Povera aesthetic, Maroon works primarily with found objects, rearranging their context to tell powerful stories. His practice serves as a poignant commentary on his lived experience—a culmination of events he has faced as a person of colour in Cape Town. Through his sculptural artworks, Maroon interrogates the unequal disposition so many experience as ‘normal life’, offering a narrative that is both deeply personal and widely resonant.

item.title: Diablo Santana
item.description: Giancarlo Diablo Santana (b. Gaborone, Botswana) is a self-taught multidisciplinary artist. Giancarlos work is centered around his personal psychological states as well universal ideas about the human experience. Through photography, painting, drawing, video, collage and digital art, Giancarlo explores the relationship between masculinity and violence through the specificity of a Southern-African context. His work raises questions about existentialism and also attempts to destigmatize conversations around masculinity, politics, culture and heritage.

item.title: Drujorn Brink
item.description: Drujorn Brink is a printmaker and artist based in Johannesburg. With a background in technical and hyper-realistic drawing, Drujorn creates art that evokes thought and highlights symbolism through the use of Christianity, South African politics, South African Coloured and Khoikhoi and Black South African culture, and personal afflictions like identity crises, worldview of tumultuous current politics and the ephemeral quality of life itself - all within being South African. Drujorn is known for his technical drawing skills, which are showcased and transferred into his printmaking. He specialises in etching and silkscreen printmaking. He aims to share the symbolism in his art with a diverse audience.

item.title: Elli Wahl
item.description: Elli Wahl was born and raised in Germany, moved to the UK for 2 years after school and have been living in Johannesburg for the past 12 years. She studied Fine Arts at Wits and used her artistic knowledge to start her own bespoke wedding-cake business.Due to the pandemic and major restrictions on events the business was closed after 8 years during which she became the top wedding-cake designer in South Africa. As she mourned the loss of her edible canvas she rediscovered painting. This process has been fuelled by ambivalence, rage, disappointment, frustration, and grief - which has led to depictions of electric excitement as death flows into rebirth and a rediscovery of the joys of texture, nuances, and movement.Her paintings are visual narratives - a juxtaposition of the despair, hopelessness, rage and frustration; and a new-found hope for passionate expression.

item.title: Christo Basson
item.description: South African artist Christo Basson is known for his finely crafted drawings and paintings that explore contemporary culture. His artworks span both figuration and abstraction, employing a rich colour palette and a wide range of media, and often incorporating mixed-media elements.Basson works with pencil, charcoal, paint, and printmaking, drawing on his strong illustration background to develop a personal visual language. Alongside his studio practice, he is the co-founder and creative director of the Cape Town–based animation production companies Bewilder and Rave Growl.He studied Visual Communication at the University of Stellenbosch and has participated in many group and solo exhibitions. Basson has worked extensively in international animation and illustration.

item.title: Diablo Santana & Moratiwa Molema
item.description: Moratiwa Ute Molema is a Motswana interdisciplinary artist whose practice unfolds across fine art, sculpture, choreography, and film. With a painterâ€™s soul and a sculptorâ€™s hands, her work bridges canvas and movement, clay and breath - shaping stories that dance between the ancestral and the avant-garde. Her visual language is interwoven with sonic landscapes, spiritual archetypes, and indigenous futurism. As an artistic director and choreographer, she has led landmark productions in Botswana and beyond.Diablo Santana (b. 1993) is an interdisciplinary artist and curator, born and raised in Gaborone, Botswana. His practice centers on destigmatizing difficult conversations around politics, masculinity, cultural heritage, and postcolonial identity within the context of Botswana and Southern Africa.Experimental in nature, his work spans painting, drawing, collage, photography, video, installation, and music production â€” often blurring the boundary between abstraction and representation. Recurring themes include personal grief, atheism, masculinity, and the psychological weight of historical memory. He currently lives and works in Gaborone, where he continues to build community through mentorship, curation, and local arts advocacy.This marks Diablo and Moratiwa's first collaborative project.

item.title: Jackson Hlungwani
item.description: Jackson Hlungwani had no formal training as an artist and learned to carve from his father who made utility items for his community.
