item.title: LAJA
item.description: Laja (Oladotun Oshilaja) if a visual artist who lives and working in Lagos, Nigeria. After completing his studies in Fine Arts at both the Yaba College of Technology, Lagos and the University of Lagos, Nigeria, he chose to pursue a full-time studio practice and explore his artistic style.Laja’s work is a manifestation of the abstract expressionist influences and expressive figurative work. Using visual metaphors to investigate ideas on existential philosophy and identity, he often uses bold strokes of paint and charcoal to explore the extensive possibilities of form, colour and line. Laja has exhibited in both solo and group exhibitions in Lagos, Nigeria including; JCAA, 2021; Tribexxla, 2021, Treehouse Lagos, 2020.

item.title: Mhlonishwa Zulu
item.description: Mhlonishwa Zulu is a contemporary South African artist, born in 2002. Storytelling has been a steadfast companion in the artist’s life since childhood, ignited by the captivating narratives woven by their cousin and uncles. Their tales - imbued with intricate details of distant lands and enigmatic figures - transported the artist beyond the boundaries of their KwaZulu-Natal environment, inviting them to explore the richness of imagination and the potential for transformation. This early exposure shaped the artist’s understanding of identity and place, inspiring an ongoing exploration of what it means to create new narratives from lived experiences.The artist’s work seeks to explore the liminal spaces between thought and action, challenge perceptions, and invite viewers to reflect on their own internal dialogues. Through Christian religious sentiments and symbolic reconciliation, they aspire to create a visual lexicon that speaks to shared experiences, illuminating the moments in between where potential resides, and where stories are waiting to be told. Through this continuous journey of artistic exploration, the artist invites others to join in pondering the profound questions of existence, identity, and interconnectedness that emerge in spaces we occupy.

item.title: Nazeer Jappie Cypress
item.description: Nazeer Jappie (b. 1998, Cape Town) is a graduate of the Cape Town Creative Academy. His multidisciplinary practice is focused on performance, sculpture and painting.Jappie’s works are predominantly self-portraits. His obsession with storytelling allows the artist to weave into different narratives and frame himself accordingly. Drawing from the repetitive performativity of everyday life, the artist looks for ways to bring attention to the absurdity of routine by intensifying its intrinsically surreal characteristics.Artist statement:“I aim to walk the line between the mundane and the absurd. In a world that is overwhelmed with excess, it is the nothingness that fascinates me. The ghosts of those moments that are not witnessed are therefore as tangible as any other unspoken secret. The spaces in which nothing happens, the imagined and the fabricated, the realm of dreams. These are the non-moments I wish to reveal.”

item.title: Asanda Kupa
item.description: B. 1981, Molteno, Eastern Cape, South Africa.Asanda Kupa’s (b.1981) work is grounded by the experiences of those forced to the periph- ery of ‘The New South Africa’; despite its great re-birth. Born in Molteno – a semi-rural village in South Africa’s poorest province, the Eastern Cape – Kupa’s scenes depict the chaos and energy of life for many of South Africa’s subjugated black population, a life that is defined by struggle and by lack of access to basic resources.Kupa is concerned with how the new political regime has failed its people – the very people who brought it to power through their own sacrifice – whilst also celebrating the self-de-termining spirit that marks a long history of civic action. Protest, spurred by grass-roots community frustration, is a central theme of his work. His series of striking crowd scenes, inspired by the Marikana mine-worker massacre of 2012, shows militant action not only as an expression of fury, but also a place of refuge and hope in post-apartheid South Africa.

item.title: Raja Oshi
item.description: Raja Oshi is a Sudanese artist now living in South Africa. Graduated from the College of Fine and Applied Art at the Sudanese University of Science and Technology in Khartoum in 1994, her journey of diaspora, and that of her family, has taken her through Norway, Wales, France and Egypt. From 2004 to present, she has settled in Pietermaritzburg where she completed a postgraduate diploma in Fine Art from the Centre for Visual Arts at the University of KwaZulu-Natal in 2006, raised a family and has continued to paint.Raja’s work is inspired by her life context and what is happening in the world. Living in Sudan, her early work depicts the situation of Sudanese women and things going on in their lives. Being part of this moved her and this came out in her paintings. Her work from that period carries the pain and the desire to change things.Her recent, depicts a new moment. Emerging from the desert literally and figuratively, as an artist, she wants to find something different in her art and in the process of making it - to get out of that world of pain, to experience, enjoy and find happiness in the painting and colour at this time in her life. Her work explores colour, texture, shape and design, drawing from the rich profusion of colour in her South African environment. Her workweaves and overlaps different materials and layers of paint to reveal the colours coming up from underneath. As she finds her own signature, this body of work radiates a stilled centeredness, a vibrant visual record of this time in her life.

item.title: Talia Goldsmith
item.description: Talia Goldsmith was born in Israel and studied art at the Kalisher school of Art. She came to South Africa in 1984 and grew up with this country. She has an inner fascination with found materials and their use, influenced by her roots (Yemen) and her life in South Africa. Talia infuses her work with unusual and unique combinations of new and recycled materials. The organic forms, texture, weaving, stitching, manipulating and human labour are influenced by her roots. She always says "Roots are the Essence.” Her work is a story that bridges between material, religion, culture and history. Her latest body of work Sysiphus incorporates a range of materials in an unlikely combination which come together in an absurd dystopian vision of the human condition. Her focus as an artist is to comment on the human condition through means and metaphors of interrogating the human form, language, spirituality and music.Talia's work forms part of collections in South Africa, Israel, Canada and New York. She has had solo exhibitions as well as group exhibitions.

item.title: Toni-Ann Ballenden
item.description: Toni-Ann Ballenden is a South African artist whose work is born from a unique and deeply personal process of deconstruction and reconstruction. Her abstract compositions are meticulously reassembled from older, unresolved works that she has obsessively cut upa cathartic act that transforms destruction into a positive creative journey.This method is rooted in her personal history and a long-standing impulse to destroy figurative drawings she deemed "not good enough." This process, influenced by feelings of being undervalued in childhood, has become a way to cope with life's challenges. Guided by the principle articulated by Louise Bourgeois that art, no less than wisdom, waits on life, Ballenden allows her lived experience to be physically and metaphorically remade in the studio.A pivotal moment in her career came in 2015 with a residency at The Bag Factory in Johannesburg, which catalyzed her shift from figurative work into abstraction. It was here that she fully embraced her process, finding a way to use the cut-up pieces of her past to build a new, abstract visual language.Ballendens work is held in high esteem, evidenced by numerous accolades and significant collections. She holds a National Higher Diploma cum laude from Wits Technikon (1993) and was the winner of the prestigious Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Award in 1992. With nine solo exhibitions to her name, her work is included in major collections such as The Astrup Fearnley Art Museum in Oslo, the Sasol Collection, the Anglo American Collection, and the SAFFCA Collection.

item.title: Henrico Greyling
item.description: Henrico Paul Greyling (b. 2001, Pretoria) is a South African multi-disciplinary artist currently living and working in Pretoria. He completed his Fine Arts degree with distinction at the University of Pretoria. Greyling’s practice spans sculpture, installation, photography, painting, and drawing, reflecting a strong engagement with materiality and process. His work is recognised for its tactile qualities, often incorporating rocks, cement, and found objects to create layered surfaces and forms. Through these materials, Greyling explores themes of memory, environment, fragility, and transformation. His practice combines technical craftsmanship with conceptual depth, producing visually striking and immersive contemporary artworks within South African art.

item.title: Shana Ellappa
item.description: Shana Ellappa (b. 1999, Johannesburg, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary artist and researcher based in Cape Town. Her practice moves between visual art, life writing, and memory work, exploring personal and collective histories through acts of reclamation. Grounded in storytelling as both method and material, she constructs counter-archives that centre lived experience and familial memory. Drawing on oral histories and embodied knowledge, her work translates these narratives into visual forms through recurring symbolic languages. Informed by African feminisms, postcolonial theory, and autoethnography, Ellappa’s practice interrogates the intersections of identity, history, and belonging. She holds a Master’s degree in Art from Rhodes University.

item.title: Lily Waterkeyn
item.description: Lily Waterkeyn (b. 1999) is a South African artist based in Cape Town. Lily completed her Bachelor of Social Science at the University of Cape Town and is currently doing an Honours in Landscape Architecture. She works with a range of mediums to create colourful paintings inspired by the range of flora and hues in landscapes. Her works articulate a deep love for the natural world and the visible and hiding colours they hold. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

item.title: Welcome Danca
item.description: Welcome S'phiwe Danca is a contemporary artist hailing from the South Coast of Port Shepstone in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Mentored by Sibusiso Duma and influenced by the late legendary artist Trevor Makhoba, Danca has forged a distinct path in the visual arts. His work is a conceptual exploration of everyday life, delving into personal memories to navigate the profound contrast between his rural upbringing and his current urban lifestyle. Danca brings these themes to life through a versatile use of mediums, including oil paint, acrylics, charcoal, and recycled materials. With extensive experience and expertise, Danca has produced a significant body of work and has been featured in numerous visual art exhibitions across South Africa and internationally, including in London, United Kingdom. His paintings are sought after by both national and international art collectors and he is frequently commissioned for new works, marking his presence on the global art scene.

item.title: Givan Lötz
item.description: Givan Lötz is a painter, sculpture and musician working in Johannesburg. Lötz is interested in spaces of emotional resonance. In his work, he manipulates the capacity for paint to render organic forms and natural cycles of growth and decay. This process forms part of a personal visual shorthand, creating a world we recognise but cannot explain.Lötz has been included in the ABSA L’Atelier Top 100 in 2012, 2013 and 2014 and Design Days Dubai in 2014 and 2015 with five residencies in the last few years from locations as far ranging as Finland, New York and Cape Town. Lötz was selected for a solo showcase at RMB Latitudes 2025 (JHB) and recently included in a prestigious institutional group show titled "Abstract" at Rupert Museum (CPT). Solo shows: Memory Exposure (2018); Unearthly (2020); Close But Not Too Close (2021); Murmurs (2022); A Middle Distance (2024) and Notes from the Fire (2025).

item.title: Oh Weetie
item.description: Tamara Weetman is a South African illustrator, designer, and lecturer based in Stellenbosch. Working under her studio Oh Weetie, she creates vibrant, narrative-driven digital illustrations inspired by everyday life, human truth and connection, music, and the places people call home. Her practice spans illustration and design, with a particular interest in storytelling, memory, and placemaking. She also writes for academic conferences and journal publications, extending her practice into research-led reflection on design, illustration, and participatory creative processes. Alongside this, she is a watercolour illustrator, and loves capturing events, moments, and environments in real time through expressive, observational drawing. Through illustration, she documents and reimagines the people, objects, and environments that shape our experiences, often combining observation, humour, and nostalgia. Her work celebrates the joys of ordinary moments and the quirky human truths that connect us. Alongside her creative practice, Tamara lectures in visual communication and holds a Master’s degree in Design. Her work has been exhibited in multiple group and solo exhibitions, her graphic design has been used internationally and locally and she continues to explore illustration as a tool for connection, reflection, and storytelling.

item.title: Selwyn Steyn
item.description: Selwyn Steyn (born 1997) completed his undergraduate degree in architecture in 2019, ending as the winner of the Pretoria Institute of Architecture design award in his year. His passion and focus however has always been visual art. His work arises from the departure point of a knowledge base grounded in spatiality and place-making. Selwyn finds parallels between spatial theory and visual cultural whilst navigating multiple mediums in his pursuit of grappling with interpretations of our individual and collective understandings of psyche, identity, perception and ideology, within the context of South Africa. Selwyn has exhibited at the ABSA gallery with BKHZ, Turbine Art Fair with RMB Talent Unlocked, No End Contemporary, UJ Art Museum, and the National Arts Festival. He was a finalist in the 2019 PPC Imaginarium and 2019 Sasol New Signatures competitions as well as a merit award winner in the 2016 edition of the Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards and the winner of the 2020 edition of UJ and MTN’s Continuing Conversations competition.

item.title: Marlise Keith
item.description: Marlise Keith (b. 1972) is known for her mixed media collages; large-scale drawings in pencil, ink and acrylics; and most recently, for her small sculptures of fabric, embroidery and found objects. Her subject matter is vast, drawing inspiration from a mental medley of horrific news headlines, colonial history, friends’ pets, psychopathology, girlhood memories, dreams, her persistent migraines, and roadside memorials. Subjects too daunting, too confused, or too subliminal to articulate in neat words and sentences, are processed through mark-making; offering an alternative “understanding” of a world that often does not make sense in traditional, logical language. This violence emerges in plentiful paint; sometimes it is suggested by the very act of mark-making itself – paper is gouged, scratched, sanded, torn, folded, and nailed.

item.title: Thelma van Rensburg
item.description: Thelma van Rensburg was born in Pretoria, South Africa in 1969. She has a B.A Honours degree in physical education from the University of Pretoria and a B.A Honours degree in psychology from Unisa. In 2004 she decided to study art full time and received her B.Tech degree in Fine Arts at Tshwane University of Technology in 2007. She completed a further Honours degree in Fine arts at the University of Pretoria in 2013 and completed a Masters of Arts degree in Fine Arts at the University of Pretoria in 2016. She completed three artist residencies through Transart Institute for creative practice in Berlin and Mexico between 2015 and 2018. She has participated in nine solo exhibitions and numerous group exhibitions throughout South Africa. Her work has featured in prestigious competitions such as Sasol New Signatures, Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards and the Sanlam Vuleka Arts competition.

item.title: Mncedisi Mkhize
item.description: Mncedisi Mkhize (b. 1996, Pietermaritzburg) is a Durban-based visual artist whose practice centres on portraiture and figurative representation. He began his artistic training at the Tatham Art Gallery under the mentorship of Mrs Pinky Nkabinde before studying Fine Art and Design at Thekwini College. Mkhize later expanded his printmaking practice at Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg. He has participated in various mural projects and group exhibitions, including presentations at KZNSA Gallery. His work explores the identities of Black people, particularly young people, within contemporary social environments, celebrating beauty, resilience, self-expression, and the complexities of everyday lived experiences and community narratives.

item.title: Takalani Mafumo
item.description: Takalani Mafumo (Taki) is a Photographer & Multi-Disciplinary Creative, b. 2001, Pretoria, South Africa | Based in Pretoria & Johannesburg, South Africa. Takalani (b. 2001, Pretoria, South Africa) is a South African multi-disciplinary creative currently based between Pretoria and Johannesburg. Holding a BA in Visual Communication from OpenWindow, with a double major in Photography and Interaction Design, they work across photography, videography, and interaction design to create evocative visual narratives that blend portraiture and landscape, drawing deeply from cinema to connect with viewers on a personal level. That foundation in both lens-based art and UX/UI design shapes everything from how they approach a frame to how they think about the experiences their work creates, bringing a rare dual fluency to their practice. Beyond photography, Takalani is passionate about film, collaborative creative work, and continually pushing into new artistic territory. They believe in making art and design genuinely accessible, and carry that belief into every project, whether through a camera, a video production, or a digital interface. Mafumo's practice is built around connection, with people, with spaces, and with the moments that pass between them. Their work is an act of memorialisation, slowing time just long enough to preserve a feeling, so that no matter how far you travel from a place or how long ago a moment occurred, you can always find your way back to.

item.title: Nondumiso Shange
item.description: Nondumiso Shange (b. 2000, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa) is a South African photographer and visual artist whose practice bridges the worlds of commercial photography and contemporary fine art. While working across fashion, editorial and advertising, Shange's personal artistic practice turns inward, using photography as a means of exploring identity, heritage and her own belonging in South Africa as a Zulu woman. Drawing from her upbringing in KwaZulu-Natal and Johannesburg, Shange creates intimate portraits that reflect on family, cultural inheritance, and the ways in which identity is shaped by both her personal and collective histories. Her work often incorporates symbolic materials, traditional garments, and carefully constructed compositions to examine themes of ancestry and selfhood. Following an art residency in Japan in 2025, Shange's practice expanded to explore xenophobia, displacement and human connection across different cities. This research-driven approach continues to inform her work, balancing documentary observation with conceptual portraiture. By navigating both commercial and fine art spaces, Shange embraces two distinct visual languages: one driven by collaboration and storytelling for clients, and the other deeply personal, rooted in lived experience and the desire to preserve and reinterpret cultural memory. Through her work, she invites viewers to consider the complexities of identity while celebrating the beauty found within heritage and developed throughout her diverse upbringing.

item.title: Andile Bhala
item.description: Andile Bhala (b. Soweto, South Africa) is a Johannesburg-based documentary and commercial photographer whose work is rooted in powerful, human-centered storytelling. Informed by his upbringing in Soweto, Bhala brings an immersive and deeply sensitive approach to documenting contemporary South African life exploring themes of identity, memory, masculinity, spirituality, and everyday resilience with striking honesty and nuance. He has exhibited extensively across South Africa and internationally. Notable presentations include Inkumbulo (Cape Town, Paris), with exhibitions at Investec Cape Town, Kiff & Marais (Paris), FNB art fair and along the Sea Point Promenade (Cape Town); Seriti at the Rise Africa Festival; and Balelihle at COOP Gallery, Nashville. His work has also been shown at the Arles International Festival (France), Jakarta, Vienna, and London, with upcoming exhibitions scheduled for London (2026), Arles (2026), and Lagos (2025). Earlier career highlights include uBUDODA at the Market Theatre Art Fair (Johannesburg) and Addis Foto Fest (Ethiopia, 2018), God Moves at RMB Art About Gallery (Johannesburg, 2022), North-West University, and Thami Mnyele Fine Art (Ekurhuleni), where he was also recognized with the Thami Mnyele Fine Art Award. Bhala’s work has been widely featured in leading publications such as Mail &Guardian, Design Indaba, Bubblegum Club, and Creative Feel, solidifying his position as a distinctive and compelling voice in contemporary visual storytelling.

item.title: Daddy Tshikaya
item.description: Daddy Tshikaya (°1986, Lubumbashi) is a visual artist trained at the Academy of Fine Arts in Lubumbashi. He has participated in numerous collective exhibitions at the contemporary art gallery “Dialogues” in Lubumbashi. In 2004, his works are part of the exhibition titled “Nguyu ya Kazi” at the Royal Museum of Central Africa in Tervuren, Belgium. Two years later, he received the first prize in the United Nations AIDS Contest. In 2009, he organised his own personal exhibition “Nani Na Nini” at the Halle de l’Etoile in Lubumbashi and at the Halle de la Gombe in Kinshasa. In 2010, his works are included in an exhibition organized by the Asbl Dialogues and the Rachel Forrest Foundation following a donation of monumental sculptures to the City of Lubumbashi, on the occasion of the celebration of its centenary. Several solo and group exhibitions in Congo and Belgium have strengthened Daddy Tshikaya’s career as a visual artist.

item.title: Georges Senga
item.description: GEORGES SENGA Georges Senga (full name Georges Senga Assani, b. 1983, Lubumbashi) is a Congolese photographic artist whose work moves between documentary and fiction, using the image to probe history and the narratives that surface through memory, identity and heritage. He graduated in human sciences from the University of Lubumbashi (UNILU) in 2009, having already begun photographing the year before. His trajectory is inseparable from the artistic scene of his home city. He was discovered during the first edition of the Picha Biennale in Lubumbashi in 2008, at a workshop led by Marie-Francoise Plissart and Sammy Baloji, and in 2010 joined the Picha art centre, where he became one of its core photographers. His first sustained series, "Empreintes", was selected by curator Simon Njami for the 2010 Lubumbashi Biennale and subsequently travelled to Tarifa, Brussels, Nairobi and Bamako. He took part in Goethe-Institut masterclasses in Bamako, Lubumbashi and Lagos between 2011 and 2013. In 2012 he produced two further series, "Une vie apres la mort" - a meditation on Patrice Lumumba, on the passage of time and on the persistence of what Lumumba continues to signify - and "Kadogos", on child soldiers. The Lumumba series was shown at the Musee national de Lubumbashi in 2013 and later at the Kampala Biennale, Addis Foto Fest and MuZee in Ostend. A Pro Helvetia research grant took him to Zimbabwe in 2014 for the project "Transit", and in 2015 he undertook a residency at WIELS in Brussels. He has also worked with the Market Photo Workshop in Johannesburg and Akademie Schloss Solitude in Stuttgart, and in 2019 participated in "Rebel Lives" at FOMU in Antwerp. In 2020 he was awarded a fellowship at the Villa Medici, the French Academy in Rome, where he developed "How a Little Pagan Hunter Becomes a Catholic Priest". The project reconstructs the life of Bonaventure Salumu, a Catholic priest who died in 1989 and who, despite his vocation, fathered a child; Senga's encounter with Salumu's daughter set the work in motion. Positioned at the crossroads of Congo's pre- and post-colonial eras, it was presented at the 7th Lubumbashi Biennale (2022) and published as a book, later shown at WIELS. Senga now lives and works between Lubumbashi and Europe, most recently based in Rotterdam.

item.title: Megan Kaylor Bosson
item.description: Meg is a curious creative based in Cape Town. She is an advocate for creative living - because life and design are so beautifully intertwined. Meg creates under two sub-brands, namely MegKaylor, which focuses on her product design career, and Silly Goose Agendas, which is is a series of playful and explorative artworks featuring allegorical figures of geese, or “silly gooses.” At the heart of the series is Silly Goose, an allegorical character representing the artist herself. Through this character, the artist captures memories, experiences, emotions, and perspectives in a whimsical yet deeply reflective manner. The human experience is a tapestry of moments - complex, layered, blurred, and at times overwhelming. Yet, amidst the chaos lies a poetic simplicity: the idea that “life is simply for living.” Meg’s work seeks to convey this duality, embracing the intricacies of human experience while distilling them into moments of playful clarity. This collection draws inspiration from Meg’s life and travels, highlighting the intersections between work and play, connections across cultures, and the simultaneous highs and lows that shape our lives. Through this collection Meg has stepped out of her comfort zone, moving beyond her usual structured UX/UI work to experiment with diverse materials and fantastical ideas - creating a playground of reflection for herself and “The Silly Goose”. The result invites the observer to engage in a similar sense of exploration - piecing together their own “puzzle” of the human experience, even if the pieces don’t seem to fit perfectly. Meg is also the cofounder of a young collective called Side Quest Studios, founded with her creative partner Tamara Weetman (OhWeetie). Through this collective, these two creatives purposefully step away from the digital world they are so often a part of, to explore playful creation though various means of print-making methods, ink work, paint and other mixed-media.

item.title: Abigale Calisse
item.description: Abigale Calisse is a South African multidisciplinary artist whose work explores generational trauma, memory, and the inherited language of domestic craft. Having lived between South Africa and Mauritius before returning home, her practice bridges geography and emotion-anchored in the shared, silent legacies carried through womanhood Working primarily in lithography and crochet, Abigale intertwines printmaking with tactile textile traditions to investigate themes of gender-based violence (GBV) and childhood trauma. Her work reflects on how trauma is not only experienced individually, but also passed down generationally-transmitted through the same hands that stitch, mend, and make. By printing lithographs on crocheted surfaces, she transforms the pattern itself into metaphor: each variation represents the shifting, cyclical nature of inherited pain and the resilience woven through it. At the core of her process is repetition-an act of quiet persistence. The meticulous, rhythmic motions of her mediums mirror the slow labour of healing Through this, her studio becomes both a site of making and a space of recovery. Each thread, each print, becomes an intimate offering-an invitation to witness, remember, and begin again

item.title: Zara Julius
item.description: Zara Julius (b. 1992) is a Johannesburg-based transdisciplinary artist whose practice spans sound, multimedia installation, performance, printmaking, and social practice. Working across research, archive, and performance, she explores Black cultural innovation, spirituality, memory, and collective forms of gathering, drawing on histories embedded in colonial archives, liberation movements, and personal memory. Her work investigates how embodied performance and sound can reshape understandings of time, affect, and historical memory. Julius has exhibited internationally at institutions including the Javett Art Centre UP (Pretoria), Akademie der Kunste (Berlin), Kunstinstituut Melly (Rotterdam), Wereldmuseum (Amsterdam), Darat al Funun (Amman), and the Weltmuseum Vienna, where she presented her debut solo exhibition Whatever You Throw at the Sea... (2023-24). She holds an MA in Fine Art by research and practice and has undertaken specialist training in documentary film and opera-making. Her work has been widely published, and her writing on "rapture" will appear in Thinking from Black: A Lexicon (Alchemy by Knopf Canada, 2026). She currently develops projects that bridge archival research, performance, and sonic experimentation.

item.title: Yasmeen Abdalah
item.description: Yasmeen Abdalah is a Sudanese visual artist, born in Qatar in 1992 and currently based in Muscat, Oman. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Painting from Sudan University College of Fine and Applied Arts, graduating in 2014. Working primarily through painting, Yasmeen explores memory, identity, displacement, resilience, and transformation, alongside the emotional and spiritual connections between humanity, nature, and the self. Deeply influenced by poetry, particularly the writings of Mahmoud Darwish, her work unfolds through layered figures, symbolic interiors, rich textures, and intuitive compositions that move between reality and imagination. Yasmeen approaches the canvas as a space of infinite possibility. Her creative process is meditative and instinctive, allowing figures, forms, and narratives to gradually emerge through layers of colour and texture. Having lived across Qatar, Sudan, and Oman, she draws from diverse cultural environments, bringing together contrasting elements such as light and shadow, nature and interior spaces, and the personal and collective experience. Through fragmented narratives and dreamlike visual worlds, Yasmeen reflects on the complexities of human experience and the capacity of the human spirit to endure, adapt, and evolve. Her work invites viewers into moments of reflection and connection, revealing the shared emotions and stories that exist beyond geographical and cultural boundaries.

item.title: Láura Viruly
item.description: Láura Viruly (b. 1997, Johannesburg) is a Cape Town-based sculptor working primarily in forged and formed aluminium, alongside installation. She completed her Master of Fine Art with distinction at the University of Cape Town in 2025.Viruly's practice explores sites of fantasy, spectacle, and cultural myth-making in South Africa, examining how colonial aesthetics, consumer culture, and inherited symbols continue to shape contemporary ideas of desire, entertainment and affluence. Drawing on autoethnographic research, she creates hollow sculptural replicas of ornamental forms and serial objects using labour-intensive metalworking techniques of 'copying', questioning the authority of the original through processes of repetition, replication, and material transformation. Her work investigates the tension between belief and artifice, revealing spectacle as both a source of enchantment and a mechanism of cultural erosion.

item.title: Chidimma Nwafor
item.description: Chidimma Nwafor (b. 1995, Onitsha, Nigeria) is a Lagos-based painter whose figurative oil paintings explore imagined memory, dreams, and the psychological space between absence and presence. Drawing from personal experience, she examines longing, sisterhood, loss, and transformation, creating dream-like compositions where memory, imagination, and reality intersect. Her work has been exhibited in Nigeria and internationally, including with Rele Arts Foundation, Kuenyehia Prize, and Mitochondrial Gallery. Nwafor was a finalist for the Art X Prize (2023) and Kuenyehia Prize (2024), and was shortlisted for the Cassirer Welz Award (2025). She holds a B.A. in Fine and Applied Arts from the University of Benin.

item.title: Bella K
item.description: Bella Knemeyer (b.1991) combines a background in sculpture (BAFA Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town), landscape architecture (MLA, University of Edinburgh) and research to explore urban narratives and material flows. Based in Cape Town, her practice traces how materials transpire spatially; how places are made, broken and mended, and how art-making may document structures and landscapes in transition as an alternative method of archiving. In February 2025 she undertook her second solo exhibition with Reservoir Here, there and everywhere, following her debut solo with the gallery, Something about this place in 2023, both in Cape Town. She was a 2023/24 National Arts Council South Africa recipient in collaboration with POOL. Her work is included in the permanent collection of the Iziko South African National Gallery, Investec Collection and Yellowwoods.
